title: Summarize the excerpt from 'EchoSystems Chrono Compendium v1.0' (chunk 14.71) about time: According to the special theory of relativity, in the high-speed particle's frame of reference, it exists, on the averag
prompt: Summarize the excerpt from 'EchoSystems Chrono Compendium v1.0' (chunk 14.71) about time: According to the special theory of relativity, in the high-speed particle's frame of reference, it exists, on the averag
true_answer: According to the special theory of relativity, in the high-speed particle's frame of reference, it exists, on the average, for a standard amount of time known as its mean lifetime, and the distance it travels in that time is zero, because its velocity is zero. Relative to a frame of reference at rest, time seems to 'slow down' for the particle. Relative to the high-speed particle, distances seem to shorten. Einstein showed how both temporal and spatial dimensions can be altered (or 'warped') by high- speed motion.
